bug_semantics: An attacker-influenced URL reaches transcribe_anything.api.transcribe(url_or_file), which passes it to audio.fetch_audio after only a startswith("http")/startswith("ftp") routing check. fetch_audio calls ytdlp_download, where src/transcribe_anything/ytldp_download.py interpolates url without quoting or validation into a single yt-dlp command string and executes that string with subprocess.run(..., shell=True). Shell metacharacters in the URL are therefore parsed as commands and run with the transcribing process's privileges (CWE-78/CWE-77 command injection); the project has no default listener, so remote exploitation requires an integration that forwards attacker-controlled URLs.
flaw_origin: The smallest origin is 7247b8c3fbdcdb625ab42389b2cc0781383e5e1c, which first added transcribe_anything/run.py and, in fetch_mono_16000_audio, placed url_or_file unquoted in an f-string youtube-dl command and immediately ran cmd with shell=True. Later commits changed youtube-dl to yt-dlp, reshaped the helper, extracted it to transcribe_anything/ytldp_download.py, and moved the package under src/; those are evolutionary edits/moves, not the origin of the flawed URL-to-shell mechanism.

evidence: First-party report https://github.com/zackees/transcribe-anything/issues/137 is still open and documents the exact current path src/transcribe_anything/ytldp_download.py, the API flow transcribe -> fetch_audio -> ytdlp_download, a benign command-substitution reproduction, affected-through-4.1.0 claim, and the required list-argv/shell=False fix. BIC: git log -L 22,31:transcribe_anything/run.py v1.0.2 resolves the vulnerable block solely to 7247b8c3fbdcdb625ab42389b2cc0781383e5e1c (https://github.com/zackees/transcribe-anything/commit/7247b8c3fbdcdb625ab42389b2cc0781383e5e1c), whose diff adds transcribe_anything/run.py:27 `cmd = f'youtube-dl ... {url_or_file} ...'` and line 28 `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, ...)`. Direct-parent proof: `git ls-tree -r a7aa39feed35b757edf9ca1fc79f99f6296ced2f -- transcribe_anything/run.py` is empty and `git grep -n -F youtube-dl a7aa39feed35b757edf9ca1fc79f99f6296ced2f` has no match; parent URL https://github.com/zackees/transcribe-anything/tree/a7aa39feed35b757edf9ca1fc79f99f6296ced2f. reasoning: The causal property is not the later filename or choice of downloader; it is concatenating the external URL into shell source and invoking a shell. Git -L and pickaxe history trace that property back through the src-layout move and helper extraction to 7247b8c3fbdcdb625ab42389b2cc0781383e5e1c, where it was first written. Its immediate parent contains neither transcribe_anything/run.py nor any youtube-dl text, proving absence. Tag-tree checks place the first affected release at v1.0.2 after safe v1.0.1; every tagged descendant examined through v4.1.1, plus version-4.1.2 main, retains the mechanism. Although e9ae5f322b4e3679c026cc65388875370c414946 briefly removed shell interpretation, it was restored before any tag and therefore is not a durable advisory fix. The upstream report remains open and current public main is still vulnerable, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are null because the case is genuinely unpatched. Finally, attribution is decided only from the true BIC commit object: it contains a human author/committer and no AI marker, supporting NOT_AI.

potential_fix.approach: Validate the caller-supplied URL against a trusted-host allowlist and resolve and block private/loopback/link-local addresses before passing it to fetch_audio/yt-dlp.
potential_fix.rationale: Host allowlisting plus SSRF-safe IP resolution prevents the attacker-influenced URL from reaching internal endpoints.
